children: Koninika Mitra joins SBS India after six years at Amazon, bringing more than two decades of experience across HR strategy, talent and organisational development

SBS India has appointed Koninika Mitra as Head of Human Resources, marking her move from Amazon after more than six years with the company. She brings over 20 years of experience across HR business partnering, talent management, people analytics, career development, performance management, compensation and organisational development.

Mitra served as HR Vertical Leader at Amazon from July 2020 to August 2026, where she led the people function across three global business verticals. Her responsibilities included HR strategy, leadership development and people-related initiatives supporting business teams.
Before Amazon, she was Corporate HR Leader at Honeywell from July 2017 to June 2020. She also served as Head of Human Resources at Max Skill First between September 2015 and June 2017.
Mitra spent more than five years at Times Internet as General Manager HR from March 2010 to August 2015. Her career also includes experience with HSBC and Lehman Brothers.
Her professional background covers HR business partnering, HR analytics, career development, performance management, compensation and organisational development across multiple industries.
At SBS India, Mitra will work with the India Leadership Team on employee experience, talent development and organisational effectiveness.

Her remit will involve people-related priorities as the organisation develops its workforce and business operations in India. Her experience across HR leadership, analytics and talent management will form part of the function's focus under her new role.
Mitra holds a postgraduate qualification in Personnel Management and Industrial Relations from XLRI Jamshedpur. She is also an alumna of Presidency University, Kolkata.

The appointment adds an HR leader with experience across technology, financial services and other sectors to SBS India's leadership team. Mitra's career spans roles involving people strategy, organisational development and workforce management.
